items.title: 11.1.2 Domains and Ranges of Secant Function (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Aaj ka sabaq chhota hai magar bohat kaam ka: secant function. Pichle sabaq ka rule yaad hai? Jahan fraction ho, wahan denominator zero nahin hona chahiye. Secant bhi ek fraction hai, aur aap dekhenge ke is ka domain bilkul tangent jaisa nikalta hai. Lekin range mein ek nayi aur dilchasp baat aayegi: secant kuch values kabhi nahin leta.

blocks.alt: Unit circle with centre O at the origin, axes X prime X and Y prime Y. It meets the axes at A(1, 0), B(0, 1), C(minus 1, 0) and D(0, minus 1). The terminal side OP, drawn as an arrow, makes angle theta with OX; P(x, y) is on the circle, M is the foot of the perpendicular PM on OX, OM = x and MP = y.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.1 (repeated from 11.1): unit circle with P(x, y) on the terminal side of θ (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text:
\[\sec\theta = \frac{1}{x},\quad x \ne 0\]
\(\Rightarrow\) terminal side \(\overrightarrow{OP}\) ko \(OY\) ya \(OY'\) (yani \(Y\)-axis) par nahin aana chahiye
\[\Rightarrow \theta \ne \pm\frac{\pi}{2}, \pm\frac{3\pi}{2}, \pm\frac{5\pi}{2}, \ldots\]
\[\Rightarrow \theta \ne (2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2},\ \text{where } n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Secant function ka domain \(= \mathbb{R} - \{x \mid x = (2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\}\)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: 11.1.1 ki tarah yahan bhi mana angles wali line kitab mein gadmad chhapi hai (\(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) aur \(\frac{5\pi}{2}\) ek doosre par). Sahi line: \(\theta \ne \pm\frac{\pi}{2}, \pm\frac{3\pi}{2}, \pm\frac{5\pi}{2}, \ldots\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Secant ka denominator wahi hai jo tangent ka: \(\sec\theta = \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{\cos\theta}\) aur \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x}\). Dono tab fail hote hain jab \(x = \cos\theta = 0\), yani terminal side \(Y\)-axis par ho. Is liye secant aur tangent ka domain ek jaisa hai.
Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: jis function ke denominator mein \(\cos\) (yani \(x\)) ho, woh \(Y\)-axis par fail hota hai: tan aur sec. Yeh dono "cos wale bhai" hain.

Ab range. Hum ne abhi dekha ke \(x\) zero nahin ho sakta, aur \(-1 \le x \le 1\). To do suraten hain:
\[0 < x \le 1 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{x} \ge 1 \Rightarrow \sec\theta \ge 1\]
\[-1 \le x < 0 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{x} \le -1 \Rightarrow \sec\theta \le -1\]
Kyun ke \(\sec\theta\) \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan wali values ke ilawa har real value leta hai,
Secant function ki range \(= \mathbb{R} - \{x \mid -1 < x < 1\}\)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Kitab \(0 \le x \le 1\) aur \(-1 \le x \le 0\) likhti hai, yani \(x = 0\) ko bhi shaamil kar leti hai. Lekin \(x = 0\) allowed nahin (\(\frac{1}{0}\) ki koi value nahin; isi liye to hum ne use domain se nikaala tha). Sahi baat yeh hai:
\[0 < x \le 1 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{x} \ge 1\]
\[-1 \le x < 0 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{x} \le -1\]
Aakhri jawab (range) par is ka koi asar nahin.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Reciprocal (ulta, yani 1 ko us number se divide karna) lene se value \((-1, 1)\) se bahar kyun chali jaati hai? Ek simple misaal: ek roti ko aadha karein to har hissa \(\frac{1}{2}\); lekin 1 ko \(\frac{1}{2}\) se divide karein to jawab 2 aata hai, kyun ke 1 mein do "aadhe" samaate hain. Isi tarah:
\(\frac{1}{1} = 1\), \(\frac{1}{0.5} = 2\), \(\frac{1}{0.1} = 10\), \(\frac{1}{0.01} = 100\).
Jitna chhota positive \(x\), utna bara \(\frac{1}{x}\). Negative \(x\) ke saath bhi yahi hota hai, bas minus sign ke saath: \(\frac{1}{-0.25} = -4\).
Is liye \(\sec\theta\) kabhi \(\frac{1}{2}\) nahin ho sakta, kyun ke us ke liye \(\cos\theta = 2\) chahiye, jo cosine ki range se bahar hai.
Interval notation mein range \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) hai. \(1\) aur \(-1\) shaamil hain: \(\sec 0 = 1\) aur \(\sec\pi = -1\). Sirf beech wala hissa \((-1, 1)\) gayab hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Kya \(\sec\theta = -1.5\) mumkin hai? Is ke liye \(\cos\theta = \frac{1}{-1.5} = -\frac{2}{3}\) chahiye. \(-\frac{2}{3}\) cosine ki range \([-1, 1]\) mein hai, to haan, mumkin hai.
Aur \(\sec\theta = 0.8\)? Is ke liye \(\cos\theta = 1.25\) chahiye, jo range se bahar hai. To nahin.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
\(\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}\) (yani \(60^{\circ}\)) par \(\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}\), is liye \(\sec\frac{\pi}{3} = 2\). Yeh \(1\) se bara hai, rule ke mutabiq.
\(\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) (\(120^{\circ}\)) par \(\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{2}\), is liye \(\sec\frac{2\pi}{3} = -2\). Yeh \(-1\) se chhota hai, phir rule ke mutabiq.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Jawab ki shakal yaad rakhein: domain ke har \(\theta\) ke liye \(|\sec\theta| \ge 1\). "Kya \(\sec\theta = 0.7\) mumkin hai?" jaise har sawal ka jawab hai: nahin.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\sec\theta = \frac{1}{x}\) ke liye \(x \ne 0\): domain \(\mathbb{R} - \{(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2} : n \in \mathbb{Z}\}\), bilkul tangent jaisa.
2. Range: \(\mathbb{R} - (-1, 1) = (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\), yani \(\sec\theta \le -1\) ya \(\sec\theta \ge 1\).
3. \(\sec\theta = 1\) at \(\theta = 0\), aur \(\sec\theta = -1\) at \(\theta = \pi\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Secant ki range \([-1, 1]\) likh dena: yeh cosine ki range hai. Secant us ka ulta hai, is liye bilkul us ke bahar rehta hai.
2. Range se \(-1\) aur \(1\) ko bhi nikaal dena. Sirf un ke darmiyan wale numbers gayab hain; kinaare shaamil hain.
3. Working mein \(x = 0\) ko allow kar dena. \(\frac{1}{0}\) kabhi mat likhiye.
